items.statement: Targeting Aakaar brand revenue share of 36-37% by end of FY27
items.quote: We would want our Aakaar brands to be around 36%, 37% in the end of year.

items.statement: Expecting revenue CAGR in higher side of 30s% and profitability CAGR around 40%
items.quote: I think we should be able to catch back the lost momentum of last year and grow at on higher side of 30s% in terms of CAGR, and profitability maybe around CAGR of 40%.

items.statement: Internal target to reduce debtor days below 130 by end of H2 FY27
items.quote: Internally, if you ask me, I am already targeting that by end of H2 it goes below 130 days.

items.statement: Expect debtor days to reduce to 180-160 by end of H2 FY27
items.quote: I think by, by end of H2, we would want to bring it down to 180 days to 160 days.

items.statement: Gross margin contracted to 51.39% in H1 FY27 from 57.88% in H2 FY26 due to forex, product mix, and sampling costs
items.quote: Gross margin stood at 51.39% in H1 '27, that is September '26, compared with 57.88% for March '26, supported by the rising share of own brands.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to improve in H2 FY27 as sampling costs lower and product mix shifts
items.quote: In the second half, it is slightly low, so our gross margins would slightly improve.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 12.71% and PAT margin 8.05%
items.quote: EBITDA presently is INR5.59 crores for September '26 and giving a margin of 12.71% compared to INR2 lakhs of September '25. PAT for September '26 is INR3.54 crores and giving the margin of 8.05%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR43.99 crores, up 72.6% YoY, best first-half sales in recent years
items.quote: The first half of FY27 has been a very important landmark day for us, especially this has been one of the best first -half sales performance in las t few years.

items.statement: Doctor base grew to 6,300+ in FY26, added 4,700+ in H1 FY27, targeting 8,000-9,000 by year-end
items.quote: Last year, we built around 6,300 plus customers. In this first half a lone, we have built around 4,700 plus customers and we are looking to close the year at least to 8,000 customers to 9,000 customers.

items.statement: Aakaar brand share 34% in H1 FY27 vs 38-39% in FY26; imported brands 64-65%
items.quote: For us, the area of focus of growth has been Aakaar brands, but in the first half typically we saw that there was slightly more pull towards the imported brands and our ratios are slightly lower for Aakaar brands at 34% vis-a-vis the last full financial year which stood at around 38% to 39%.

items.statement: Targeting 60-40 imported to own brand mix long-term
items.quote: So, the current trend is slightly tilted this year towards the international brands, and we intend to keep this ratio at around 60-40.

items.statement: Hair transplant device (IFUE) development budgeted over last 2-3 years, nearing CDSCO test license filing
items.quote: We have already allocated funds on the R&D over period, so it has started happening over 2, 3 periods, then the device has started getting final shape in last quarter, and we are close to test license.

items.statement: Distributor network expanded to 40+, targeting 100 in 2 years for better last-mile delivery
items.quote: Currently we have already appointed 40 plus distributors across India, and we are looking to keep expanding this distributor network at least to 100 in the coming two years so that our last mile delivery improves.

items.statement: Debtor days 219 in H1 FY27 vs 206 in H2 FY26; targeting 130-150 days by FY27 end or H1 FY28
items.quote: Debtor days presently are 219 days for September '26 compared with 206 days for March, and we are concentrating on bringing down this, debtor number of days.

items.statement: Working capital stressed due to imported brand inventory, MOQs, forex, geopolitical risks; expect improvement with distributor model
items.quote: So yes, there would be slightly stressed working capital in the near future, but I think as our policies in terms of distribution network and collection from doctors and payment through distributor changes, our working capital would be much better and much optimized.

items.statement: Forex (euro/dollar) and European supply cost increases hit cost of goods; sampling costs also embedded in COGS
items.quote: The biggest hit has been the forex change. The cost of goods from the company side also has increased due to the supplies in Europe, because most of our brands that come from Europe, there is slightly increased cost of goods.

items.statement: Recurring revenue 92-93% of total; field force ~120 people; B2B model with doctor stockkeeping driving debtor days
items.quote: About 92% of our revenue is recurring, and with a field force that remains at around 120 plus people, we believe this model can deliver strong growth with operating leverage over the coming years.

items.statement: LETYBO (US FDA botulinum toxin) targeting 75% market share vs Botox; local competitor Gufic has pricing advantage from local manufacturing
items.quote: We are targeting a market of botulinum toxin, that is Botox, and our local competition also comes from brand Gufic, where Gufic is slightly having advantage in terms of pricing because of local manufacturing. But we are targeting the 75% of market and taking market share from Botox.

items.statement: Hair transplant device (IFUE) prototype ready, filing test license with CDSCO; regulatory approval process underway
items.quote: We have purchased rights of development from Dr. Kuldeep, who developed the first prototype, and we are onwards to the first stage of filing test license for the hair transplant automated device with CDSCO.

items.statement: FotoFinder dermatoscopy/trichoscopy devices showing great feedback; higher-value Medicam and ATBM models in pipeline
items.quote: We are seeing great feedback and sales in this this portfolio, and we are looking forward for incremental sales in the FotoFinder range, the Fotofinder Medicam and FotoFinder ATBM, the higher value devices could add to our revenue.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (wars, oil crisis) impacting European manufacturing costs and supply chain for imported brands
items.quote: Ever since we got list ed last year, even while we filed our RHP, the India -Pakistan war and then the Russian war and now the oil crisis that is happening has impacted the manufacturing costs in Europe, and that is impacting the cost of goods to us.

items.statement: H1 FY27 marketing spend INR3.4 crores vs full FY26 INR2.76 crores; includes non-recurring FAHA conference costs
items.quote: In the first half, majorly we have invested to a tune of INR3.4 crore s in marketing, vis -a-vis the last year full year spend of INR2.76 crores.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR1.05 crores in H1 FY27 vs INR16.2 crores in H2 FY26
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalent stood at INR1.05 crores compared with INR16.2 crores of March '26.

items.statement: Planning direct-to-consumer website and e-commerce listings to capture prescription leakage; full rollout by end of FY27
items.quote: We are also working on our direct-to-consumer website, so that our consumers that are getting the products purchased from doctors can directly come and purchase the brands from our own website.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% CAGR revenue growth over next three years from FY26 base
items.quote: the targeted growth, which we are expecting is going to be about in 30%, 35% year-on-year growth over next three years at a CAGR level.

items.statement: Has confirmed visibility of 60-62% of targeted H2 FY27 revenue
items.quote: whatever targeted number that what we have taken, we already have a confirmed visibility of about 60% to 62% of the balance H2 to go.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 20-21% H-o-H and 30.7% Y-o-Y in H1 FY27; confident of sustaining margins in H2
items.quote: the EBITDA for the same period of H -o-H grew by about 20%, 21%, which is fro m INR 16.2 crore to INR 19.5 crore. And for year-on-year, it grew by 30.7%.

items.statement: Built proprietary AI content platform with Google and Seed Dance; animation production cost reduced to one-tenth of traditional
items.quote: we have built our own proprietary content management platform and AI content platform in collaboration with Google, with Seed dance, where we are basically going to -- or we are we are already creating animation content.

items.statement: Animation tech ready; can produce 20-25 minute episode in 6-7 hours vs 2-3 weeks traditionally
items.quote: today, as we speak on the capability, what we have built on the tech side, we are able to produce one episode of 20 , 24 minutes, each in like flat six to seven hours.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: TV ~45%, Film & OTT ~48-49%, Digital ~6.5-7%; digital share to increase over next three years
items.quote: in FY26, the contribution from TV was about 45% . From film and OTT business, that's how we bundle and we do a segment wise, was about 48%, 49%. And digital was only close t o 6.5% to 7%.

items.statement: Works with all major broadcasters (Sony, Colors, Zee, Star), OTT platforms (Netflix, Jio, Amazon), and studios (T-Series, Viacom)
items.quote: we pretty much work with all the industry leaders , be it a broadcaster like a Sony, Color, Zee, Star, or OTT platform like Netflix, Jio, Amazon, or a studio like T-Series, Viacom.

items.statement: Film model: fixed 10% producer fee + 3-4% allocated team cost = 14-15% locked margin; IP share 40-50% after studio pre-sale
items.quote: we take our fixed 10% fee on that. And if, as I said, if all the -- after all the costs getting recouped, if the movie does well in theatr e, then you share revenues.

items.statement: Receivables INR 59 cr at Sep 30, 2026; expected collection by Dec 2026; operating on 90-120 day cycle; no bad debts in 25 years
items.quote: if you see end of 30th September, the consolidated receivables are at about INR 59 crores, which will be collected by December end 2026.

items.statement: Liabilities decreasing; paying creditors early for better deals; no debt concerns raised
items.quote: the liability is not increasing. In fact, the liability has been decreasi ng that we are been paying to our creditors and getting a better deal from them.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with T-Series for Hindi films; co-production structure with major South producer for Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam films
items.quote: we have a strategic partnership with our studio partner T-Series. And similarly, we have created a structure with one very big and popular producer down south. Through that relationship, we will be venturing and getting into producing movies in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam.

items.statement: Regional film ticket size defined at INR 5-7 crore; Gujarati film already on floor; Diplomat Part 2 prepping for next year
items.quote: for us, a ticket size in regional is defined not more than INR 5 crore to INR 7 crore. So if the movie falls into this financial discipline of INR 5 crore to INR 7 crore , and the script is great, and something which we can greenlit, we will go ahead.

items.statement: Launching animation YouTube business by mid-to-late January 2027; 30-35 original IP characters registered; Balveer animation rights owned in perpetuity
items.quote: The target what we have taken internally is to launch this animation YouTube businesses by about Jan mid to Jan end, which will go live with.

items.statement: Will deploy excess cash in business growth and pay dividends to shareholders
items.quote: deployment will be in the company growth and also shareholders because we also need to value that and there will be dividends, which will get paid to the shareholders to build their confidence and also create value for the shareholders.

items.statement: Conservative 30-35% CAGR guidance accounts for project timing risks and IPO capital deployment lag
items.quote: there are end of the day it has its risk i n terms of projects, sometimes going to the next quarter, there might be . So we are also keeping that thing in mind.

items.statement: Creative leadership structured by genre (fiction, non-fiction, comedy, crime); most leadership including CFO with company 12-15+ years
items.quote: all our creative all our leadership, including our CFO , and everyone the company, most of them have been with us for more than 12 to 15 years.

items.statement: New IP 'Game Changer' with Madhavan launching in UAE market; shoot starting December 2026; company will own IP piece
items.quote: we recently announced our new IP or a new show called the Game Changer with Madhavan, which is like a business reality show to be launched in UAE market. So it's already out. We'll start the shoot in December.

items.statement: Expanding into UAE market with 'Game Changer' show; planning global expansion
items.quote: this year, we're entering UAE with our show. So we will, of course, need money to expand.

items.statement: Differentiation: 25-year track record across fiction, non-fiction, crime, kids, films, OTT; institutional execution capability across all major broadcasters, platforms, studios
items.quote: very few production companies have produced long running primetime television, nonfiction formats, crime programming, children franchise, feature films, OTT series, while maintaining relationship across almost every major broadcaster, pla tform and studio

items.statement: Oncology revenue expected to cross 50% share next year and 60% in 2-3 years
items.quote: So maybe in next year onwards, we will be crossing that 50%. So in couple of years' time, we will be crossing that 60% marks what you are expecting from oncology -- we are expecting from oncology.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 35%+ expected to be maintained in FY28
items.quote: So last year al so it was 40% plus year-wise, and this year also we are on 35% plus. So that growth rate will be also maintained in this year and the coming year

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 30% currently, moving to 34-35% with full API integration in couple of years
items.quote: once we have the integrat ion done with the API, then it will be moving ahead to maybe 34%, 35%, or even more. But t hat will take a couple of years' time, as I mentioned, because we need to integrate the in-house APIs then

items.quote: whatever we hav e done in terms of partnerships, as you rightly mentioned, that will be crossing around 70 within this year, considering right now we are sitting on 69

items.quote: We have already given them the dossiers. Rou ghly around 16 dossiers are there currently under MIMS approval in different GCC countries and other markets nearby

items.statement: 351 oncology dossiers shared globally, 191 submissions, 22 marketing authorizations granted

items.quote: as on d ate, if you see already out of 22, we have commercialized around 6 of the molecules which we h ave already received in terms of the approvals from the EMA or other regulatory bodies

Eight products have already been commercialized, w hile two of our seven CEP applications have been approved and the remaining applications continue to progress through the regulatory review

items.statement: Current blended EBITDA 28%, oncology ~30%, non-oncology ~26%
items.quote: See, right now the EBITDA is around 28%, which is you can see with more or less an equal contribution from oncology and non-oncology, revenu e-wise. So if we consider, then maybe it will be around 30% for the oncology and 26% for the non-oncology, what we are we can get it

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA expected around 30%, moving to 34-35% with API integration over couple of years
items.quote: See, the current business model, as long as it con tinues for oncology, so that will become something around 30%. But once we have the integrat ion done with the API, then it will be moving ahead to maybe 34%, 35%, or even more

We are bound by which are practical margins as a manufacturer, and so there i s no impact or hardly any we see any impact in the coming day
